verdict.rationale: Keycloak documents client-credentials service accounts for machine-to-machine access, which an agent can use. It pairs these with role-based policies and fine-grained, resource-level authorization services to restrict what such a client can do. Credentials can be provisioned programmatically through dynamic client registration, the Admin CLI and the REST API, and tokens can be revoked or introspected. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of per-client OAuth scope restriction or token audience limiting, any agent-specific credential guidance, and independent hands-on corroboration of least-privilege agent credential setups.
